items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: And the Jaws was the bass drum player. I didn't like the way Jaws played.

ctx.x: Well, how did he work with a bass drummer, man? How did the bass drum and the snails work in the street? Would he work steady with one guy, would they work up things or not together?

No, well, look, Cottrell, he played with the Excelsior band all the time, you know. And the Jaws was the bass drum player. I didn't like the way Jaws played. He was playing good marches and things. Marches played a band, terrific playing the marches. I hate to say that, but I didn't like the way he played bass drum. He didn't play the police beat, because he didn't play the jazz beats. He didn't play the strings. You know, he played the strings, you know, boom, boom, jump, jump, jump, like that. And the mother…
Ray Allen. Which one? You mean the young one? Yeah, Ray Allen. Sonny Allen.
